classification.capability: Declared read/write effect hazards (my reads versus your writes) with explicit coverage
classification.basis: No surveyed README was found that states read-set validation with explicit coverage. The nearest counterparts are TeamBus (published contracts with consumers blocked until they commit; conflict check over contract-consumer and import relations) and Orchestune (shared-contract risks), which are consumer-side dependency checks and so close to read effects; whether they state coverage was not established from README text and nothing was reproduced. Read-set validation exists in the literature (S-Bus, arXiv:2605.17076v1), so this is an applied-to-Git-worktrees and Claude Code claim, not a novel technique

Radar (Jake-Network/radar) and other tools report missing evidence, so unknown as a first-class result is not a differentiator by itself and is dropped as a standalone claim by founder decision of 2026-10-24. Only the combination is retained as a candidate: an Article 13 compatibility class on every output, pairwise classification that includes unknown, declared read/write hazards and a declared-versus-observed receipt. The combination is untested and each part is small and copyable

classification.capability: Order-independence evidence via bounded replay certificates (at most four operations)
classification.basis: No counterpart found; merge-queue bisection (Refinery, SVRF) is post hoc and answers a different question

classification.capability: Declared-versus-observed envelope receipt with stated observation coverage
classification.basis: No counterpart found among surveyed tools; unverified for tools whose behavior beyond the README was not read. Classified exact-path receipt, Article 13 class 1-syntactic, never a guarantee

priorArtPass.boundedClaim: In a dated pass on 2026-10-24 (query set recorded in the radar snapshot), no surveyed README of a shipped Claude Code plugin or coordination tool was found that states read-set validation with explicit coverage, or that provides order-independence evidence from bounded replay. TeamBus and Orchestune describe consumer-side or shared-contract checks that may be near-neighbors; their READMEs were read, their behavior was not reproduced. This is absence within the surveyed set, not a statement about the whole market, not a claim of novelty over the literature, and not evidence of user demand.

Native Claude Code features (agent teams, cross-session messaging, agent view, /batch, hooks) are taken from the research digest and orchestrator-verified facts, not re-fetched in this pass

Literature was not re-surveyed. The references listed under literatureReferences were identified through search excerpts or an abstract page on 2026-10-24, not read in full. The percentage figures from the 2026-10-24 research digest that are not listed there (agent self-reports over-claiming shared resources by 32 to 49 percent; 92 to 95 percent of freshness-guard blocked races being benign) are unverified and must not be cited

The search used 17 queries, a name-and-description filter over 315 official marketplace plugins and several queries that returned 0 results; READMEs of TeamBus and Orchestune were not read beyond the summaries recorded here

entries.title: Gas Town: multi-agent workspace manager (Witness, Refinery, convoys, hooks)
entries.sourceDate: README read via gh api on 2026-10-24; MIT, 18,509 stars, pushed 2026-10-24
entries.relationship: Reported coordinator (Mayor) plus git-worktree-backed hooks, a per-rig Witness that monitors workers, detects stuck agents and triggers recovery, a Deacon patrol supervisor, convoys with stall detection, escalation routing and a Refinery described as a Bors-style bisecting merge queue with verification gates. It launches and manages agents, which Agent Braid never does. Liveness, recovery and merge-queue verification are broader than anything Agent Braid plans (behind). The README describes no declared read/write effect analysis or order-independence evidence. Candidate interoperation: Agent Braid as an evidence step consumed by a verification gate; not designed or tested.
entries.decision: Retain as a surveyed comparator for the M4.6 orchestrator-coordination track; no integration, comparison or superiority claim. Behavior was read from the README only and was not reproduced.

entries.title: Beads: git-backed, dependency-aware agent issue memory
entries.sourceDate: README read via gh api on 2026-10-24; MIT, 28,160 stars, pushed 2026-10-24

It is task memory and claiming, not file or effect analysis. A durable claim register is behind Beads for task state; Agent Braid's SPEC-059 ledger must not duplicate it without a documented reason (G2).
entries.decision: Retain as a surveyed comparator for the M4.6 orchestrator-coordination track; no integration, comparison or superiority claim. Behavior was read from the README only and was not reproduced.

entries.title: DriftWatch: tree-sitter symbol-graph conflict detection across worktrees
entries.sourceDate: README read via gh api on 2026-10-24; 2 stars, pushed 2026-09-15
entries.relationship: README reports watching every active worktree, building tree-sitter symbol graphs, cross-referencing changed symbols against usages in other worktrees, an optional bring-your-own-key LLM severity layer, and feeding a conflict into a running agent's context. This is symbol-level overlap detection from observed code, which is finer than Agent Braid's exact-string resource model (Agent Braid is behind on semantic granularity). It does not appear to model declared effects, coverage or order independence. Low adoption and unreproduced.
entries.decision: Retain as a surveyed comparator for the M4.6 orchestrator-coordination track; no integration, comparison or superiority claim. Behavior was read from the README only and was not reproduced.

entries.title: OpenWeft: batch scheduling by declared file manifests, with recovery
entries.sourceDate: README read via gh api on 2026-10-24; MIT per README badge; stars not recorded in this pass; pushed 2026-09-09 per search listing
entries.relationship: README reports plans that declare files to create, modify or delete, overlap detection across manifests, phased scheduling, worktree execution through Codex CLI or Claude Code, and recovery of interrupted work. It states that decisions use predicted file changes, not a semantic dependency graph, and that an agent can change files outside its manifest. Declared-footprint pre-flight is therefore parity; it also launches agents, which Agent Braid does not.
